text: Austin Fred JAMM 475 Script Treatment 2 September 2018 -Think Happy Thoughts on Sunday (Working)- 	Kirby Peter’s prefers to spend his Friday nights getting high with his friends or watching the newest movie on Netflix or even just playing board games with his parents. What else is a sixteen-year-old boy supposed to do? Oh, right, girls. Kirby Peters definitely does not “do” girls. In fact, he hasn’t even kissed one. The opportunity just hasn’t presented itself yet. All of this was about to change, thanks to Kylie James. 	Kylie is a fair looking young woman who just moved into the neighborhood with her dad. On the first day she is moving in, Kirby saw his “opportunity.” He bolted out the front door and crossed the street to introduce himself to the first woman he found physically attractive, as he grabs the box she is carrying. For two awkward sixteen-year-old kids, they talk to each other as though they are kindred spirits. After only 15 minutes of talking and moving boxes, Kirby scores an invite to dinner with Kylie and her dad that night. 	The dinner is pleasant. Kylie’s father likes that Kirby is a fan of the Denver Broncos and has a 4.0 and plays the guitar. And Kylie and Kirby’s connection becomes even stronger when they realize they both read the same book series. As the evening winds down, Kirby says good night to Kylie’s father and Kylie walks Kirby to the door. As he steps through the door frame, Kylie pulls him back by the arm and whispers to meet her at her bedroom window at midnight. Kirby is shocked, but plays it cool and agrees. 	The exchange later that night is brief. They both agree on the fact that neither of them has ever met someone like the other. Then they agree that they would date. Then they agree that they won’t be one of those couples that makes out in public, like ever. Then they agree to be each other’s first kiss. 	Then the camera lands on something simple like a leaf or cotton, and the wind picks the object up, and blows it through the air “into” the next scene, which is four years later. 	Kirby and Kylie’s relationship has lasted all the way into their third year of college. They live together in an apartment off of campus. And they HATE each other right now. They are screaming and fighting about their future together, which leads to a fight about religion and philosophy, which leads to Kylie sobbing and Kirby punching the wall on his way out the door. They have been fighting like this for a few weeks now, but this fight is the last one for Kylie. 	The camera tilts down to the doormat, then the camera tilts up to show a passage of time, and to show Kirby frantically knocking and coughing at Kylie’s door. 	Kylie opens the door as Kirby coughs bloody harshly into his sleeve. He sees the blood and collapses into Kylie’s arms. Then she quickly gets him to the car and the camera settles on a leaf as Kylies skids out of the parking lot, causing the leaf the drift into the night sky. 	Kirby lays in a hospital bed, looking ghostly. A pastor sits beside Kirby’s softly crying mom as Kirby and he share a philosophical conversation about life and death. They talk about the loneliness of it all. Then they talk about the togetherness and the pastor leaves on a happy note. He exits and nearly bumps into Kylie, who walks in the room. Kirby’s mom leaves to give them some privacy. It’s awkward at first. They both try to talk at the same time. And again. But then they laugh and start talking about cancer and school and Kylie’s new boyfriend. There is no bitterness between them, and Kirby openly claims to be happy that Kylie moved on…even though he is dying. Eventually the conversation shifts back to what Kirby and the pastor spoke about. Kirby could not shake off what he said when him and the pastor were speaking. He had never really considered that he would die completely ALONE. This is doubly shocking for him, given his current circumstances. He is panicking over it, in fact. Kylie is doing her best to calm him down, but Kirby cannot stop his sobbing. Kylie runs out of things to try and say, and decides to just hold Kirby as tight as she can. His sobbing slows eventually and Kylie stares in his eyes. She gives a beautiful monologue about Kirby’s fear of being/dying alone, reassuring him that, no matter what, she will always be with him and he will never be alone. 	Day passes to night and Kirby’s mom says good night and leaves. Kylie gets up to leave shortly after. Kirby was able to get into a good mood again, but Kylie reminds him that she will always be with him, no matter what. Kylie leaves and Kirby is left to his dark hospital room, with a shitty TV playing a shitty sitcom. Kirby doesn’t care about any of that though. He feels a warm happiness come over him and he closes his eyes and sees a montage of all the times he was “together.” As the montage progresses, the sound of Kirby’s heart rate monitor becomes increasingly audible. The beeps slow. The montage ends with Kirby gently opening his eyes to see absolutely no one. He is alone. Fade to black as Kirby’s POV eye droops shut. The beeps stop. END.
